- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day peaks) — cap forecast overshoot at 2x the 18-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds 3x historical mean, apply mean reversion: cap forecast at 2x historical max or 1.5x 30-day rolling average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to smooth transitions — apply smoothing filter: average last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast slope.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model underestimates — add 5–10% to forecast to capture latent momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 1.5x historical mean, model often underestimates — increase forecast by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
